criteria.criterion: Derive AoS and SoA address/traffic models for a position-only update and a whole-record consumer, including padding, cache-line assumptions and the different identity of a record after splitting fields.
criteria.scope: Representation/traffic proof and changed whole-record workload
limits: Cache lines are a stated model; actual traffic counters were not observed.

criteria.criterion: Implement a staged SoA update and an equal-contract AoS version generated from a shared field list; distinguish token-driven generation from runtime or language reflection.
criteria.scope: Generated field-list AoS/SoA and staged updates

criteria.criterion: Enumerate small signed input products and all failing record positions with an independent integer oracle; verify untouched columns and kill skipped-update and premature-prefix-commit mutants.
criteria.scope: 22143 signed-product cases, all four rejection positions, untouched columns
limits: Finite x/velocity {-1,0,1}, ticks {0,1,10}, plus extreme rejection boundaries.

criteria.criterion: Measure warmed and cold working sets, vectorization reports, code size and conversion costs under equal overflow semantics. Report crossover uncertainty; demonstrate a whole-record workload where SoA can lose.
criteria.scope: 672 actual measurements, conversion costs, code/assembly and whole-record reversal
limits: Eviction-conditioned runs do not establish physically cold caches. No affinity/frequency control, second processor or confidence interval.

criteria.criterion: Transfer to an array-of-small-tiles layout with an optional cold column. Derive row/column bounds and schema evolution before changing the implementation; C diagnostics do not verify field-list semantic consistency.
criteria.scope: Three-wide tiles, eight rows, optional cold field and bounds

criteria.criterion: Derive the representation invariant for empty, inline and heap states and the exact invalidation events for borrowed views; explain why alignment of a character array alone does not permit arbitrary typed C objects.
criteria.scope: Empty/inline/spill invariants and byte-storage permission
limits: No arbitrary typed objects in byte storage.

criteria.criterion: Implement all capacity transitions and a fixed-capacity alternative using allocator injection, with strong append rejection and exactly-once resource release under move/reset.
criteria.scope: All byte-buffer transitions and fixed-capacity alternative

criteria.criterion: Inject every allocation failure and test capacity16/17, maximum128, zero append, self move, nonempty destination, repeated reset and compact after truncation; compare byte sequences with an independent list model.
criteria.scope: 33540 length/failure cases; compact/move boundaries; allocation accounting
limits: Host malloc failure is injected, not an observed exhausted host allocator.

criteria.criterion: Compare the documented LLVM inline-vector idea with this C byte representation and a typed-union alternative. Measure owner footprint, allocations, copy traffic and spill hysteresis rather than claiming universal zero overhead.
criteria.scope: Actual byte versus typed owner size/copy/allocation/threshold observations
limits: Explicit payload stores are counted separately from total compiler/hardware memory traffic.

criteria.criterion: Integrate dod.small_buffer with an erased closure byte capture: define which values can be encoded, which callbacks own external resources and why memcpy of a self-referential capture is not relocation.
criteria.scope: Actual T70 byte storage consumed by T69 encoded closure and actual T66 allocator
limits: Current seven-profile consumer campaign pins actual T70 producer and T66 allocator. The owner context is stable and borrowing is synchronous; no general self-referential relocation or reverse prerequisite edge.

criteria.criterion: Derive low7-bit addition, high-bit combination and saturation masks, proving which intermediate carries can occur and why neighboring lanes remain independent.
criteria.scope: Low-bit carry/high-bit saturation derivation

criteria.criterion: Implement the unsigned SWAR expression and an independent scalar oracle without relying on char signedness, endian memory reinterpretation or vector extensions.
criteria.scope: Unsigned packed implementation plus scalar model

criteria.criterion: Exhaust all65,536 lane input pairs in every position and with neighboring boundary lanes, then add deterministic mixed-lane random words; kill ordinary packed-add and inverted-overflow-mask mutants.
criteria.scope: All65536 pairs in each lane;524288 neighbor-boundary cases;100000 mixed words
limits: Finite32-bit word contract; not every pair of32-bit words.

criteria.criterion: Compare scalar and SWAR code under equal saturation semantics at multiple optimization levels, checking generated instructions and a changed16-bit-lane derivation. Distinguish source-level branchlessness from timing guarantees and ISA support.
criteria.scope: Unsigned16 and signed16 derivations plus six compiler/optimization timings and assembly
limits: Source branchlessness is not a constant-time security guarantee.

criteria.criterion: Prove both directions of the dense/rank bijection and distinguish stable address, stable logical identity, stable iteration order and owner lifetime.
criteria.scope: Dense/rank proof and distinct address/identity/order/lifetime rules

criteria.criterion: Implement swap-erased dense IDs with typed slot storage, generation admission and retirement; implement a two-page extension without moving live payload objects.
criteria.scope: Actual DSparse, two fixed typed pages and finite-generation retirement
limits: Two pages are embedded and fixed capacity. A separately allocated growable-page variant needs its own allocation-failure protocol.

criteria.criterion: Explore all add/remove sequences up to length7 over four IDs against an independent live-set model, checking stale and foreign-owner handles, last-row removal and pool exhaustion.
criteria.scope: 2396744 add/remove prefixes, all issued tokens, bijection and live foreign owner
limits: Alphabet is explicitly add four values/remove latest associated token, not arbitrary pointer inputs.

criteria.criterion: Transfer to a payload owning a resource and a consumer holding a raw pointer. Define destruction and invalidation, then show why generation checks do not revoke that pointer or authorize concurrent reclamation.
criteria.scope: Exactly-once owned resource destruction and defined reused-slot raw-pointer counterexample
limits: Raw pointer observation uses still-live int slot storage; it never dereferences a destroyed external resource. No concurrent reclamation claim.

criteria.criterion: Derive entity-to-table/row and table-row-to-entity invariants, query mask semantics and the distinction between stable entity ID and invalidated row references.
criteria.scope: Bidirectional table-row/entity invariants and query masks

criteria.criterion: Implement migration with destination admission before source removal, swap-row repair and transactional query updates; implement required/excluded-mask query selection and versioned cache invalidation.
criteria.scope: Admission-before-removal, cache masks/version and real typed-handle adapter

criteria.criterion: Enumerate create/migrate/update sequences against an independent per-entity dictionary, inject destination-full and arithmetic rejection, and diagnose lost-entity and stale-row-map mutants.
criteria.scope: 4374 independent recycled-entity prefixes plus rollback, full and arithmetic boundaries
limits: Finite6-step three-operation scripts, plus separate four-command atomic batch cases.

criteria.criterion: Compare sparse-set and archetype storage under query-heavy and mutation-heavy workloads, including migration copies, cache maintenance and iterator invalidation. Compose with typed stable handles under a changed deletion/reuse policy.
criteria.scope: Actual sparse-set/archetype query/mutation experiments and recycled stable-handle composition
limits: Two-live-entity successful workload; whole-world staging cost retained; not complete same-API performance equivalence.

criteria.criterion: Derive persistence as multiple observable versions with shared immutable subgraphs, distinguishing it from durable storage and from a mutable object with a const pointer.
criteria.scope: Persistence versus durability/const and graph sharing

criteria.criterion: Implement leaf-to-root path copying, an explicit zipper reconstruction and failure rollback without mutating published nodes; state allocator ownership and snapshot lifetime.
criteria.scope: Leaf-to-root path copy, explicit zipper and rollback

criteria.criterion: Inject failure at every cloned-node ordinal, compare all8 cells of every retained root with independent array snapshots, and recompute reachability and sharing from roots.
criteria.scope: 66429 successful histories/265716 allocation cuts; every root/cell; independent graph census
limits: All indices{0,3,7}, values{0,1,-1}, length<=5; not unbounded histories.

criteria.criterion: Analyze fresh-node work, retained-node space, stack depth and region reclamation latency; implement a bounded reference-count alternative with exactly-once reclamation for a shared child and explain why it is not concurrent safe by itself.
criteria.scope: Actual shared-child RC, operation budget, stack records and reclamation timing
limits: Single-threaded acyclic ownership; step budget does not bound external destructor elapsed time.

criteria.criterion: Transfer to a tree with owned string leaves and a clone callback that can fail. Define rollback for already cloned resources and compare the documented persistent-collection Clone requirement with C programmer discipline.
criteria.scope: Owned string leaves and all clone/node allocation failure boundaries
limits: No language-enforced Clone relation; trusted callbacks obey ownership contracts.

criteria.criterion: Derive bitmap rank as the population count of preceding bits and prove compact-child count/order invariants; distinguish trie-prefix, full-hash and actual-key equality.
criteria.scope: Bitmap rank and prefix/hash/equality distinction

criteria.criterion: Implement lookup/update with collision buckets and path copying, then deletion with defined empty-node normalization and immutable prior snapshots.
criteria.scope: Persistent update/deletion, empty normalization and old snapshots

criteria.criterion: Exhaust keys0Ã¢â‚¬â€œ31 and insertion/deletion permutations for collision pairs and differing bitmap positions; compare each version with an independent dictionary and inject every clone failure.
criteria.scope: 1024 ordered key-pair deletions and4105 custom-key/collision observations with failure cuts
limits: Original bounded32-key model and fixed8-key custom collision bucket.

criteria.criterion: Analyze hash quality, collision-bucket growth, retained versions and pointer/bitmap costs under equal contracts. Transfer to an attacker-selected constant hash and specify bounded denial-of-service behavior without claiming constant worst-case lookup.
criteria.scope: Custom dictionary, attacker-selected constant hash, linear collision comparisons and capacity rejection
limits: Dedicated synthetic keys; bucket ninth insert rejects after8 comparisons. No worst-case constant-time claim.

criteria.criterion: Prove ordered-DAG sequence semantics, cached length consistency and ownership of shared leaves; distinguish byte, codepoint, grapheme and line coordinates.
criteria.scope: Ordered immutable DAG, length/sharing and byte/scalar/grapheme distinction
limits: Grapheme segmentation is explicitly not implemented by scalar-index edits.

criteria.criterion: Implement transactional leaf/concat/flatten and byte-index/split operations, including empty boundaries and shared subgraphs without cycles.
criteria.scope: Leaf/concat/flatten/index/split and transactional splice

criteria.criterion: Implement gap-buffer and piece-table editing with complete capacity and source-lifetime contracts; drive identical insert/delete scripts through all representations and an independent flat oracle.
criteria.scope: Identical243 five-operation scripts through rope/gap/pieces/flat model, every rope snapshot retained
limits: 1215 current sequences plus retained snapshots; bounded128 bytes/64 nodes.

criteria.criterion: Investigate chain depth, rebalancing, fragmentation and retained backing storage using adversarial concatenation and edit locality; derive a balance criterion from the inspected rope paper without importing its measurements as this lab results.
criteria.scope: Chain depth, actual copied rebalance, Fibonacci criterion, fragment/retention statistics
limits: Midpoint-copy reconstruction is not the paper forest-rebalancing algorithm; root balance does not imply every descendant balanced.

criteria.criterion: Transfer to UTF-8 scalar-index edits and invalid byte sequences. Define validation, coordinate conversion and snapshot ownership, then demonstrate a case where byte equality alone does not establish the requested text operation.
criteria.scope: Strict UTF-8 scalar offsets/invalid sequences and atomic edits
limits: Scalar indexing is not normalization or grapheme-aware editing.

limitations: Cold-cache observation is not established by eviction conditioning.
Fixed embedded two-page pool does not implement growing page allocation.
T69 consumer aggregate receipt must be refreshed after current additions; actual capture code and separate timing receipts remain unchanged.
